subject: Re: Renewal - Conditional price-hold & milestone-linked credits
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@coresys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: conditional price-hold & milestone credits

Evan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our notes, CoreSys is targeting a renewal that keeps unit pricing stable for the first 6 months while you finalize the multi-region rollout. You asked whether we can: (1) hold current rates for an initial period, (2) provide a small safety buffer of credits for burst usage, and (3) build in a true-up cadence tied to product milestones rather than strict monthly consumption.

Quick recap of what I need from you to pull together an internal proposal:
- Confirmation of the expected commit horizon (12 vs 24 months)
- Targeted baseline v burst ratio for Q4 (rough numbers are fine)
- Any legal constraints from CoreSys on conditional pricing language (CC: legal@coresys.com)

I attached last quarter's usage report so you can confirm the baseline numbers on our side. I’ll loop in Ben from Commercial to draft a conditional amendment that aligns with your ask. Goal: get to a signed amendment that preserves your rate for first 6 months, includes a 10k-credit buffer for bursts, and ties rate adjustments to the milestone checklist you mentioned.

Available to meet Thurs or Friday afternoon PT if you want to walk through a strawman.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Renewals — Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
Attachments: usage_report_Q2.csv
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@coresys.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@coresys.com, CoreSys Legal <legal@coresys.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: conditional price-hold & milestone credits

Mina —

Appreciate the follow-up and the usage file. Quick answers below: 
- Commit horizon: preference for 12 months with the option to extend after milestone 2.
- Baseline v burst: for Q4 we expect baseline ~75% of current commit, with potential short-term bursts up to +40% around new feature launches (we'll try to keep those short).
- Legal constraints: we can accept conditional pricing tied to delivery milestones but legal wants objective milestone definitions and a maximum exposure cap. They asked me to request a draft amendment and a clear limit on credits/credits expiry.

If you can share a draft amendment and an outline of the cap trade-offs (e.g., size of the credit buffer vs. guaranteed baseline volume), that will help us move quickly. Meeting Friday 2pm PT works for me.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Liu
Sr. Manager, Cloud Procurement — CoreSys
evan.liu@coresys.com
Attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion: conditional price-hold & milestone credits

Mina / Karthik —

Notes from Evan's reply: they want a 12mo primary commit with an option to extend; baseline ~75% and up to +40% bursts; legal wants objective milestones and a cap on exposure. Proposed commercial construct (strawman):

1) Conditional price-hold: hold existing unit rates for first 6 months post-amendment. After month 6, rates can reprice only if the agreed milestone checklist isn't met (see below).

2) Credit buffer: provide a 10,000 token-credit pool for burst usage in Q4. Credits expire at the end of the 12mo term. We cap the total credit liability at 20k tokens for the term to satisfy legal exposure limit.

3) Milestone-triggered true-up: define 3 delivery milestones (M1: multi-region infra readiness; M2: production traffic >= X% baseline for 2 consecutive weeks; M3: GA feature set). If CoreSys hits M1+M2 by month 6, price-hold remains for months 7–12. If they miss M1+M2, we implement a modest repricing tied to overage bands.

4) Reporting & audit: weekly usage exports + one joint monthly review for first 3 months.

Action items: Mina to draft amendment (term sheet + legal language) and include two alternative cap levels (20k cap vs 35k cap with smaller hold). I can model P&L impact on our side if you want to propose both options.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachments: none
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@coresys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, CoreSys Legal <legal@coresys.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion: conditional price-hold & milestone credits — draft attached

Evan —

Thanks for the clarity. Attached is a short draft amendment (proposed_amendment_draft.docx) plus an executive summary PDF that walks the two concession options:

Option A (Conservative liability):
- 12mo term, price-hold for months 1–6 at current rates
- 10k credit buffer (expires at term end), liability cap 20k
- Milestone checklist: M1 + M2 required by month 6 to retain months 7–12 hold

Option B (Accelerate & incentivize):
- 12mo term, price-hold for months 1–4; if M1+M2 achieved by month 4, extend hold through month 12
- 15k credit buffer, liability cap 35k, but includes a modest uplift on committed volume after month 6 if not met

We tried to keep legal-friendly language for objective milestones and an explicit cap on credits. Please review with your counsel and let us know which option your team prefers. If we get a thumbs-up, Ben and I will route the amendment to our legal for a two-party redline and aim to have a signable doc within 7 business days.

Next steps:
- Evan: confirm option preference + any alternate cap you'd accept
- Legal (CoreSys): high-level comments on objective milestone wording
- We (Redwood): produce final redline draft and updated SOW if needed

Meeting reminder: Wed 8 Sep 2pm PT for final alignment (calendar invite sent).

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Renewals — Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
